First, navigate to the directory containing the PDF files using the `cd` command. For example, if your PDF files are in a directory called `pdfs`, you can navigate to it using:
```
cd pdfs
```
Next, use the `find` command to search for PDF files in the directory and its subdirectories. For example, to search for all PDF files in the `pdfs` directory and its subdirectories, you can use:
```
find . -name "*.pdf"
```
This command searches for all files (`.`) with the extension `.pdf` in the current directory and its subdirectories.
Next, use the `pdftotext` command to extract the text from the PDF files. For example, to extract the text from a PDF file called `document.pdf`, you can use:
```
pdftotext document.pdf
```
This command creates a text file with the same name as the PDF file, but with the extension `.txt`, containing the extracted text.
Finally, use the `grep` command to search for relevant text in the extracted text files. For example, to search for all occurrences of the word "taboo" in the extracted text from all PDF files in the `pdfs` directory and its subdirectories, you can use:
```
grep -r "taboo" ./*.txt
```
This command searches for the word "taboo" (`"taboo"`) recursively (`-r`) in all text files (`./*.txt`) in the current directory and its subdirectories (`.`).
